curation.lead:
Fettah Tamince is a Turkish billionaire and the founder and chairman of Rixos Hotels, a luxury hospitality chain headquartered in Turkey. Documents produced under the EFTA subpoena establish that Jeffrey Epstein had contact with Tamince's office as early as November 2010, when someone forwarded Epstein the contact details for Tamince's secretary Sebla — noting that Epstein's party had stayed at a Rixos property in Antalya [Finding #1192]. Seven years later, in June 2017, Epstein dispatched at least two women to a ten-day Basic Therapist Training Program at Rixos Premium Belek in Antalya, arranged directly through Tamince's personal office [Finding #265][Finding #1195].

The 2017 training was brokered by Sultan Bin Sulayem, who wrote to Tamince's office describing one of the women as "the personal masseuse at the private Spa of our friend Jeffery Epstien" and instructing staff to "train her on all the treatments" [Finding #1190][Finding #1194]. Sulayem forwarded a passport for the Russian national identified as Lina to Tamince's office [Finding #1190]. Lesley Groff, Epstein's executive assistant, handled payment logistics and coordinated arrival dates with Tamince's PA Sebla Soydan Bora, Director of the Chairman's Office [Finding #1195]. Epstein paid 5,230 EUR for the stay, confirmed via a Visa charge [Finding #1195].

According to a 2026 public statement, Tamince said he never met Epstein personally and attributed the arrangements to Sulayem's request: "Sultan bin Suleiman is my friend, he asked for something, and we implemented it" [Finding #1198]. He stated that his PA Sebla handled the matter during his absence in Astana. A review of the documentary record shows more than 30 emails addressed to or copying Tamince's name, with his personal office — not a general reservations desk — coordinating the program and receiving passport copies for the participants [Finding #1198]. Analysis of the Foreign Agents Registration Act database returned no results for either "Tamince" or "Rixos," though Turkey has 195 registered foreign principals; the absence does not establish a legal violation, as FARA applies only to agents acting at the direction of a foreign government [Finding #397].

sections.title: The Rixos–Epstein Connection
sections.content:
The earliest documented link between Tamince's office and Jeffrey Epstein dates to November 2010, when Epstein received the direct contact information for Tamince's secretary, with the sender noting that Epstein's group had previously stayed at a Rixos property in Antalya [Finding #1192]. This establishes a prior point of contact inside Tamince's personal office well before the 2017 training arrangement.

The June 2017 program was hosted at the Land of Legends Spa, with accommodation at Rixos Premium Belek on an all-inclusive basis, running from approximately June 20 to July 4, 2017 [Finding #1190][Finding #1195]. Sultan Bin Sulayem's introduction email described one participant as Epstein's "personal masseuse" and asked Rixos staff to train her comprehensively [Finding #1190]. Women's names were redacted in the produced documents; their passports were transmitted to Tamince's office prior to arrival [Finding #265].

Coordination flowed through Sebla Soydan Bora, Director of the Chairman's Office and personal assistant to Tamince, who corresponded directly with Lesley Groff and with Epstein himself on logistics, payment, and arrival scheduling [Finding #1195]. Groff handled payment via Visa card; initial Amex attempts failed because remote payment was not supported [Finding #1195]. The final confirmed charge was 5,230 EUR [Finding #265][Finding #1195]. Epstein also asked in the email record whether a second assistant should accompany the first so "she will be teaching the others after she learns" [Finding #1194].

sections.title: Sultan Bin Sulayem as Intermediary
sections.content:
Sultan Bin Sulayem, the Dubai-based logistics and ports executive, was the operative link between Epstein and Tamince. Sulayem forwarded the Russian participant's passport to Tamince's office and personally directed Rixos staff to provide comprehensive training [Finding #1194]. His email to Tamince's office, dated June 5, 2017, described Epstein as "our friend" — EFTA02344064 — language consistent with the broader email corpus in which Sulayem refers to Epstein in familiar terms across more than 6,800 documents [Finding #1190].

Sulayem was copied on subsequent logistics emails alongside Tamince's PA, positioning him as a continuing point of coordination rather than a one-time introducer [Finding #1194]. The investigation database records both a social and a financial connection between Tamince and Sulayem, though the documentary basis for the financial tie has not been fully evidenced at this stage.

sections.title: Tamince’s Public Account
sections.content:
According to a 2026 public statement, Tamince said he never met Epstein personally, that Sulayem had asked a favor as a friend, and that his office implemented the request during his absence in Astana [Finding #1198]. He attributed responsibility for the arrangements to his assistant Sebla.

Records show over 30 emails in which Tamince's name appears in the header — either as direct addressee or in office communications — and the coordination was handled by his Director of Chairman's Office rather than a general hotel reservations channel [Finding #1198]. Passport copies for participants were routed to Tamince's personal office [Finding #265]. Examination of the documentary record does not confirm or contradict the claim that arrangements were handled at a staff level without Tamince's direct awareness; the evidence establishes that his office handled the logistics but does not contain communications directly from Tamince himself in the corpus reviewed [Finding #1198].

sections.title: FARA Registry Absence
sections.content: Analysis of the Foreign Agents Registration Act database returned no results for either "Tamince" or "Rixos" [Finding #397]. Turkey has 195 registered foreign principals, the nineteenth-highest country total. Analysis of this absence does not establish a legal violation — FARA registration is required only when an entity acts at the direction of a foreign government or political party — but it is noted given Tamince's documented connections to Turkish government-adjacent networks and the presence of Rixos properties in multiple jurisdictions with state-linked partnerships [Finding #397]. This finding is classified as an inference at medium confidence.

open_questions: Did Tamince receive, read, or act on any of the 30+ emails addressed to him regarding the 2017 training program, or were all communications handled exclusively by Sebla Soydan Bora without his knowledge?

What is the documented basis for the financial connection between Tamince and Sultan Bin Sulayem beyond the hotel arrangement — are there corporate co-ventures, shared investments, or payment flows that establish the financial tie?
Were there any prior or subsequent training programs at Rixos properties for Epstein-associated individuals, given that the 2010 contact establishes a relationship predating 2017?

Is there a relationship between Tamince's Rixos operations and Turkish state entities (sovereign wealth funds, Tourism Ministry contracts, or state-linked financiers) that would bear on the FARA absence noted in Finding #397?

Epstein asked whether a second assistant should be sent so "she will be teaching the others after she learns" — were additional individuals trained at Rixos or elsewhere using techniques from this program?

applicable_models.rationale: Tamince's office provided a material service — training and accommodation — to Epstein through an established hospitality channel. The available evidence does not establish where on the enabler gradient Tamince falls: his PA's statement that she responded during his absence could place him in the "willfully blind" or "unwitting" category; the fact that his personal office received passport copies and coordinated directly could support a higher position on the gradient. The evidence is insufficient to resolve this without access to Tamince's internal communications or testimony.

Sultan Bin Sulayem functioned as a bridge between Epstein and Tamince, leveraging his personal friendship with both to facilitate the 2017 arrangement. The Sulayem–Tamince–Epstein triangle is a documented instance of the bridge pattern: Sulayem held relationships with both parties and used that position to route a request that neither party would have addressed directly.
